title: Gain/Phase Margin, Sensitivity Waterbed (S+T=1), Luenberger State Observers & Bryson's Rule for LQR

blocks.x: 1. Why it matters

This is the bridge module before Step 2.6 (`05-control.T2.06`). Trial-and-error PID tuning breaks down when your plant has a flexible shaft resonance, unmeasured velocity states, or multiple coupled degrees of freedom like the underactuated Furuta pendulum. Measuring **Gain Margin (GM)** and **Phase Margin (PM)** on the open-loop transfer function $L(s) = P(s)C(s)$, respecting the algebraic constraint $S(s) + T(s) \equiv 1$ (which explains Bode's **waterbed effect**), estimating unmeasured states with a **Luenberger observer** (the deterministic half of a Kalman filter), and normalizing **LQR cost matrices $(Q, R)$ via Bryson's Rule** gives you systematic, first-principles control design for Step 2.6. Already know this? Take the Skip test or the Ladder Gate test in section 7 first.
2. Intuition first

blocks.caption: Margins are read off this picture: gain where the phase crosses, phase where the gain crosses.

blocks.x: Why does any negative-feedback loop go unstable if you crank the gain too high? Because every Closed-Loop transfer function has $1 + L(j\omega)$ in its denominator! If the loop transfer function $L(j\omega) = P(j\omega)C(j\omega)$ ever hits magnitude $|L| = 1$ ($0\text{ dB}$) at the same frequency where its phase lag reaches $-180^\circ$, then $L(j\omega) = -1$, the denominator $1 + (-1) = 0$ blows up, and negative feedback turns into a self-sustaining oscillator! **Phase Margin ($\text{PM}$)** quantifies how many degrees of safety buffer you have above $-180^\circ$ at the $0\text{ dB}$ crossover frequency $\omega_{gc}$. Second, **Sensitivity** $S = \frac{1}{1+L}$ measures how much disturbances get through, while **Complementary Sensitivity** $T = \frac{L}{1+L}$ measures how much sensor noise gets through—and because $S(s) + T(s) \equiv 1$ at every frequency, you cannot make both zero at the same frequency (**the waterbed tradeoff**). Third, a **Luenberger observer** runs a virtual copy of your plant $\hat{x}_{k+1} = A_d\hat{x}_k + B_d u_k + L_{\text{obs}}(y_k - C\hat{x}_k)$ in software and nudges it using sensor prediction error. Finally, **Bryson's Rule** takes the guesswork out of LQR tuning by setting $Q_{ii} = 1 / x_{i,\max}^2$ and $R_{jj} = 1 / u_{j,\max}^2$ so meters, radians, and newton-meters are normalized to dimensionless percentages of their maximum allowable swings!
3. Formalization

items.x: **Loop Transfer Function $L(s) = P(s)C(s)$, Crossover $\omega_{gc}$ & Phase Margin ($\text{PM}$):**
At the **gain crossover frequency** $\omega_{gc}$ where $|L(j\omega_{gc})| = 1$ ($0\text{ dB}$), the **Phase Margin** is:

blocks.x: Robust servo loops target $\text{PM} \in [45^\circ, 65^\circ]$ and **Gain Margin** $\text{GM} = -20\log_{10}|L(j\omega_{pc})| \ge 6\text{ dB}$ at the $-180^\circ$ phase crossover $\omega_{pc}$. Time delay $\tau_d$ ($\text{s}$) eats phase margin linearly with frequency: $\Delta\phi(\omega) = -\omega\tau_d \cdot \frac{180^\circ}{\pi}$.

items.x: **Sensitivity $S(s)$, Complementary Sensitivity $T(s)$ & Waterbed Identity:**

blocks.tex: S(s) = \frac{1}{1 + L(s)}, \quad T(s) = \frac{L(s)}{1 + L(s)}, \quad S(s) + T(s) \equiv 1

blocks.x: Peak sensitivity $M_s = \max_\omega |S(j\omega)|$ measures worst-case disturbance amplification and guarantees minimum distance $1/M_s$ from the critical point $-1 + j0$ (require $M_s < 2.0 = +6.02\text{ dB}$).

items.x: **Luenberger State Observer, Scalar-to-Matrix Kalman Gain Bridge & Bryson's Rule for LQR (`DARE`):**

**Observer Update & Matrix Kalman Filter Bridge:** Given discrete plant $(A_d, B_d, C)$ and observer gain $L_{\text{obs}}$, estimation error $e_k = x_k - \hat{x}_k$ evolves as $e_{k+1} = (A_d - L_{\text{obs}} C)e_k$, which converges to zero iff all eigenvalues of $(A_d - L_{\text{obs}} C)$ satisfy $|\lambda_i| < 1$. When process noise covariance $Q_w$ and sensor noise covariance $R_v$ are known (`00-foundations.T2.00f`), the **Linear Kalman Filter** chooses the optimal observer gain $K_k$ at each step by generalizing the 1D variance ratio $K = \frac{\sigma_{\text{pred}}^2}{\sigma_{\text{pred}}^2 + \sigma_{\text{meas}}^2}$ into matrix form:

blocks.tex: P_k^- = A_d P_{k-1} A_d^\top + Q_w, \qquad K_k = P_k^- C^\top \left(C P_k^- C^\top + R_v\right)^{-1}, \qquad P_k = (I - K_k C)P_k^-

items.x: **Augmented Disturbance Observer:** A constant load torque is not in $(A_d, B_d, C)$, so an observer that models only the plant must trade steady-state bias against bandwidth. Append the disturbance as an extra state with $d_{k+1} = d_k$, giving $A_{\text{aug}} = \begin{bmatrix} A_d & B_d \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $C_{\text{aug}} = [C\ \ 0]$; the innovation then depends on $d$, so the disturbance is observable, its estimate follows $\hat d_{k+1} = \hat d_k + \ell_i r_k$ with $\ell_i$ the integral gain, and subtracting $\hat d_k$ leaves the nominal controller a plant that looks disturbance-free at steady state.

**Bryson's Rule & Discrete Algebraic Riccati Equation (`DARE`):** To minimize $J = \sum (x_k^\top Q x_k + u_k^\top R u_k)$ given maximum acceptable state deviations $x_{i,\max}$ and actuator limit $u_{j,\max}$:

blocks.x: In Step 2.6 (`05-control.T2.06`), calling `P = scipy.linalg.solve_discrete_are(Ad, Bd, Q, R)` solves for the steady-state cost-to-go matrix $P$ backwards in time, yielding the optimal constant feedback gain row vector $K_{\text{lqr}} = (R + B_d^\top P B_d)^{-1} B_d^\top P A_d$ (`u = -K_lqr @ x`).
4. Worked example

**Predict first (before you run it):** Commit to four numbers before the script runs. (1) What phase margin does $L(s) = \frac{100}{s(0.01s + 1)}$ have at $\omega_{gc} = 78.615\text{ rad/s}$? (2) What is $|S(j\omega_{gc})|$ there, and is it above or below $1$? (3) What are Bryson's weights for $x_{\max} = 0.05\text{ m}$, $\theta_{\max} = 0.10\text{ rad}$ and $u_{\max} = 5.0\text{ N}$ — and what is the observer's spectral radius for $A_d = [[1, 0.001], [0, 0.99]]$, $C = [1, 0]$, $L = [[0.19], [9.0]]$? Two tells: a margin of $-128.17^\circ$ means the $+180^\circ$ was dropped, and $Q = [20, 10]$ means the maximum deviations were not squared.
Compute the Phase Margin $\text{PM}$ and peak sensitivity $M_s$ of an open-loop servo transfer function $L(s) = \frac{100}{s(0.01s + 1)}$ at its gain crossover $\omega_{gc} = 78.615\text{ rad/s}$, verify $S(j\omega) + T(j\omega) = 1$, construct Bryson's LQR weights $(Q, R)$ for a cart-pendulum ($x_{\max} = 0.05\text{ m}, \theta_{\max} = 0.10\text{ rad}, u_{\max} = 5.0\text{ N}$), and verify Luenberger observer convergence.

blocks.text:
import cmath
import math

def loop_transfer(omega: float) -> complex:
    s = 1j * omega
    return 100.0 / (s * (0.01 * s + 1.0))

w_gc = 78.61513777574233  # Exact frequency where |L(jw)| = 1.0 (0 dB)
L_gc = loop_transfer(w_gc)
assert math.isclose(abs(L_gc), 1.0, rel_tol=1e-6)

pm_deg = 180.0 + math.degrees(cmath.phase(L_gc))
S_gc = 1.0 / (1.0 + L_gc)
T_gc = L_gc / (1.0 + L_gc)
assert cmath.isclose(S_gc + T_gc, 1.0 + 0.0j, rel_tol=1e-12)
assert math.isclose(pm_deg, 51.8273, abs_tol=1e-3)

# Bryson's Rule for x_max = 0.05 m, theta_max = 0.10 rad, u_max = 5.0 N
Q_diag = [1.0 / (0.05 ** 2), 1.0 / (0.10 ** 2)]
R_00 = 1.0 / (5.0 ** 2)
assert math.isclose(Q_diag[0], 400.0) and math.isclose(Q_diag[1], 100.0) and math.isclose(R_00, 0.04)

# Luenberger observer error matrix M = Ad - L*C for Ad=[[1, 0.001], [0, 0.99]], C=[1, 0], L=[[0.19], [9.0]]
M = [[1.0 - 0.19, 0.001], [-9.0, 0.99]]
tr = M[0][0] + M[1][1]
det = M[0][0] * M[1][1] - M[0][1] * M[1][0]
disc = cmath.sqrt(tr * tr - 4.0 * det)
rho_obs = max(abs(0.5 * (tr + disc)), abs(0.5 * (tr - disc)))
assert math.isclose(rho_obs, math.sqrt(0.8109), rel_tol=1e-9) and rho_obs < 0.91
print(f"PM={pm_deg:.2f} deg, |S(jw_gc)|={abs(S_gc):.3f}, Q_diag={Q_diag}, rho_obs={rho_obs:.4f}")

5. Exercise

Suppose your servo loop has Phase Margin $\text{PM} = 51.83^\circ$ at gain crossover $\omega_{gc} = 78.615\text{ rad/s}$, and you add a communication/filtering transport delay of $\tau_d = 0.005\text{ s}$ ($5.0\text{ ms}$), which subtracts $\Delta\phi = \omega_{gc}\tau_d \cdot \frac{180^\circ}{\pi}$ degrees of phase without changing $|L(j\omega_{gc})|$. Compute the phase loss $\Delta\phi$ in degrees and the new Phase Margin $\text{PM}_{\text{new}} = \text{PM} - \Delta\phi$. Verify $\Delta\phi = 22.5216^\circ$ and $\text{PM}_{\text{new}} = 29.3057^\circ$ ($\pm 10^{-2}$).

items.x: **If your result differs:** Convert $\omega_{gc}\tau_d = 78.61514 \times 0.005 = 0.393076\text{ rad}$ into degrees by multiplying by $180 / \pi$ ($22.52^\circ$).

[`exercises/05-control.T2.05a/`](../exercises/05-control.T2.05a/) turns this section into a test. `starter.py` holds seven holes: `phase_margin_deg` (with the loop's lag **unwrapped** - `cmath.phase` reports +160 for a 200 degree lag), `phase_loss_deg`, `st`, `gain_crossover` (bisection, and a `ValueError` when the bracket never crosses), `bryson_weights` (squared), `observer_spectral_radius`, and `lqr_gain` from the Riccati fixed point. Edit it, then run the tests the way CI does:

The tests are behavioural: the worked loop's margin must be $51.8273^\circ$ while a loop lagging $200^\circ$ must report **−20** (the naive principal value reports +340); `S + T = 1` at four frequencies; the crossover must bisect to $78.615\text{ rad/s}$ and refuse a loop that never crosses; Bryson's weights must be $[400, 100]$ and $0.04$; the observer radius must be $0.9005 < 1$; and the LQR gain must stabilise a model whose open loop already sits at $0.99$. The transfer suite shapes the **shared arm's elbow** with a PD law on its real inertia and damping, checks the crossover is a true $|L| = 1$, prices one plant tick of delay against the margin it carries, places an observer's error poles at $0.8$ and $0.9$ and **measures** the error falling at $0.9$ per tick, and runs a Bryson-weighted LQR gain until the joint comes to rest. Five planted faults - `pm_no_unwrap`, `pm_no_complement`, `st_t_inverse`, `bryson_linear`, `lqr_ap_at` - each fail the test named for them; `lqr_ap_at` is the transposed-Riccati slip that leaves the closed-loop radius at $0.99999$ and is only visible when the loop is run.

items.x: **The 5 ms delay in degrees.** $\omega_{gc}\tau_d = 78.61514 \times 0.005 = 0.393076\,\text{rad}$, and $0.393076 \times 180/\pi = 22.52^\circ$. A pure delay leaves $|L(j\omega_{gc})|$ at $1$, so $\omega_{gc}$ itself does not move.

**Why the new margin is a subtraction.** The delay adds lag, so it *subtracts* from the margin: $51.8273^\circ - 22.5216^\circ = 29.3057^\circ$. Still positive, so the loop is stable - and now below the $45^\circ$ floor, which is why $5\,\text{ms}$ of filter lag is not a detail on a $78.6\,\text{rad/s}$ loop.

**The unwrap, if you also want the general function.** `cmath.phase` returns $+160^\circ$ for a $-200^\circ$ lag; subtract $360$ before adding $180$, or a loop past the critical point reports $340^\circ$ of safety instead of $-20^\circ$.

**The other numbers in the block.** $S + T \equiv 1$ holds at any $L$, including the crossover's $1.144$; Bryson over $0.05\,\text{m}$, $0.10\,\text{rad}$ and $5\,\text{N}$ is $[400, 100]$ and $0.04$; and the observer's error matrix $A_d - LC$ has radius $0.9005 < 1$.

**What the suite refuses.** `gain_crossover` raises `ValueError` when the loop has no crossover to report: a magnitude that never crosses unity (a constant $10$) and a first-order low-pass that only reaches it at $\omega = 0$ are both refused rather than given an invented frequency.

blocks.x: Break it on purpose
Inject the phase-wrap slip the exercise plants (`pm_no_unwrap`), keeping the same loop and $\omega_{gc}$:

items.x: **Inject:** compute the margin as `180 + degrees(cmath.phase(L))` on the principal value, without unwrapping the loop's lag into $(-180^\circ, 180^\circ]$.

**Symptom:** a loop lagging $200^\circ$ at crossover reports $\text{PM} = +340^\circ$ instead of $-20^\circ$, while the worked loop's own $51.83^\circ$ still comes out right because its lag is only $-128.17^\circ$ — the fault hides until a margin is actually negative, which is exactly when it matters.

**Diagnose:** $+340^\circ = -20^\circ + 360^\circ$, so the reported margin is a full turn away and exceeds the $180^\circ$ a margin can physically reach. A gain error or a misplaced $\omega_{gc}$ would move the number inside the $0\text{–}180^\circ$ band instead of out of it, and the delay sweep would jump by $360^\circ$ at the moment the loop crosses $-180^\circ$.

**Fix:** wrap the lag to $(-180^\circ, 180^\circ]$ before adding $180^\circ$, then prove it on both sides: the $200^\circ$ loop must read $-20^\circ$, and the worked loop with $\tau_d = 5\text{ ms}$ must still read $\text{PM}_{\text{new}} = 29.31^\circ$.

`[Concept: sensitivity_complementary_waterbed_tradeoff]` Why is it physically impossible to make both disturbance sensitivity $|S(j\omega)| \ll 1$ and sensor-noise transmission $|T(j\omega)| \ll 1$ at the **same** frequency $\omega$?

**A.** Because $S(j\omega) + T(j\omega) \equiv 1$ at every frequency; therefore we shape $|L(j\omega)| \gg 1$ at low frequencies ($S \approx 0, T \approx 1$ for tracking/disturbance rejection) and $|L(j\omega)| \ll 1$ at high frequencies ($T \approx 0, S \approx 1$ for noise attenuation).
**B.** Because microcontrollers only have 32-bit floats.
**C.** Because $S(j\omega)$ is always negative.
**D.** Because Bode plots stop at $100\text{ Hz}$.

`[Concept: luenberger_observer_and_brysons_lqr_weights]` In a Luenberger observer $\hat{x}_{k+1} = A_d\hat{x}_k + B_d u_k + L_{\text{obs}}(y_k - C\hat{x}_k)$, what do we call the measurement residual term $r_k = y_k - C\hat{x}_k$?
**A.** The innovation (or output prediction error).
**B.** The actuator saturation limit.
**C.** The Gain Margin.
**D.** The process noise covariance.

`[Concept: luenberger_observer_and_brysons_lqr_weights]` What matrix must have all its eigenvalues strictly inside the unit circle ($|\lambda_i| < 1$) for a discrete-time Luenberger observer's estimation error $e_k = x_k - \hat{x}_k$ to converge to zero?
**A.** $A_d - L_{\text{obs}} C$
**C.** $C^\top C$

`[Concept: luenberger_observer_and_brysons_lqr_weights]` Using Bryson's Rule $R = 1 / u_{\max}^2$, compute the scalar control weight $R$ (in $\text{N}^{-2}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}$, tolerance $\pm 10^{-9}$) for a motor with maximum torque $u_{\max} = 2.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.

`[Concept: luenberger_observer_and_brysons_lqr_weights]` In LQR tuning, if your robot tracks the reference too sluggishly and uses very little motor current, how should you adjust the control penalty $R$ relative to the state penalty $Q$?
**A.** Decrease $R$ (make control effort "cheaper" relative to state error $Q$), which increases feedback gain $K$ and closed-loop bandwidth.
**B.** Increase $R$ by $1000\times$.
**D.** Invert the sign of $K$.

`[Concept: augmented_kalman_disturbance_observer]` A constant load is appended as an extra state with $\hat d_{k+1} = \hat d_k + \ell_i r_k$. With $\ell_i = 40\ \text{s}^{-2}$, innovation $r_k = 5.0\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}$ and $dt = 1.0\ \text{ms}$, compute the per-tick change $\Delta\hat d = \ell_i r_k\,dt$ (tolerance $\pm 10^{-12}$).
`[Concept: augmented_kalman_disturbance_observer]` Why does appending a constant-disturbance state reject a steady load better than an observer that models the plant alone?

**A.** The augmented model makes the disturbance observable through the innovation, so its estimate converges to the true constant and is subtracted; an unaugmented observer has no state to hold that value and settles with a bias.
**B.** Because adding a state increases the sample rate.
**C.** Because $A_{\text{aug}}$ is always stable.
**D.** Because the disturbance covariance replaces $Q_w$.

blocks.x: 8. Common mistakes

head: Symptom
Root cause
2-minute fix
rows: Looked only at $lvert T(jomega)rvert $ (closed-loop tracking Bode plot) and missed a dangerous $+12text{ dB}$ sensitivity peak in $lvert S(jomega)rvert $
Relying on $T(s)$ alone hides near-instability when $L(jomega)$ passes close to $-1 + j0$.
Always plot all **Gang of Four** transfer functions ($S, T, PS, CS$) and verify $max_omega lvert S(jomega)rvert  < 6text{ dB}$ ($2.0times$).
Solved continuous-time `solve_continuous_are(A, B, Q, R)` but ran the resulting $K$ at a slow discrete sample rate $T_s$
Continuous ARE ignores sample-and-hold phase lag and discrete control weighting.
Discretize $(A, B) to (A_d, B_d)$ at sample period $T_s$ and call `scipy.linalg.solve_discrete_are(Ad, Bd, Q, R)` (Step 2.6).
Set $Q = I_4$ without Bryson normalization on a state vector mixing millimeters and radians
A $1text{ mm}$ error and a $1text{ rad}$ ($57.3^circ$) error received identical weight!
Always express states in consistent SI units ($text{m}, text{rad}, text{m/s}, text{rad/s}$) and normalize $Q_{ii} = 1/x_{i,max}^2$ via Bryson's Rule.
